open_points.subject: operation refusal semantics vs multi-step write operations
open_points.text: "A refusal writes nothing" ... and operations such as `public_op:runs.start_run` have `State impact: `start_run`; `record_run_progress`` while "Internal error. A failed store call changes nothing ... the module returns it as `internal_error`"
open_points.question: If a later store call in the same public operation fails after an earlier store call already succeeded, must the operation still return `internal_error`, and are those earlier writes allowed to remain?
options: Treat `internal_error` as a refusal that must leave no writes at all (add compensation/rollback across prior successful calls)
Allow partial progress from earlier successful store calls to remain; `internal_error` only guarantees the failing call wrote nothing
open_points.default_guess: Allow earlier successful writes to remain and return `internal_error` for the failing later call only.

open_points.subject: `get_repair_view` trial execution scope
open_points.text: A15 rule 6 says repair includes "its trial cases and executions", while `get_repair_view` specifies "one page ... of the current contract version's trial cases" and "the current implementation's trial executions"
open_points.question: Should repair-view trial executions include only the current implementation, all implementations of the current contract version, or all implementations across the slot’s contract versions?
options: Only the current implementation’s trial executions
All trial executions for the current contract version
All trial executions for all contract versions of the slot
open_points.default_guess: Only the current implementation’s trial executions (as written in `get_repair_view`).

open_points.subject: `store.open_store` temporary-file cleanup target
open_points.text: `public_op:store.open_store` says: "Temporary files under the data directory are removed" and A18 says "On start, temporary files ... are removed; nothing else is."
open_points.question: What exact filename patterns/locations count as "temporary files" for deletion at start?
options: Only files created by store atomic-write protocol (known temp naming convention)
Any file in dedicated temp subdirectories only
Broad heuristic cleanup of unrecognized transient files under data directory
open_points.default_guess: Delete only files created by the store’s own temp-file naming convention (or dedicated temp area) to satisfy "nothing else is removed".
